name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body: In addition to its standard rules, each Battle Forge scenario has two random tables that add additional Victory Point-scoring opportunities for players that vary each time the scenario is played. Mission Modifiers add additional scoring opportunities based on the position of a player’s models on the table. Achievements add additional scoring opportunities based on a player’s actions taken on the battlefield. Players should roll a d6 to randomly determine Mission Modifiers and Achievements before the beginning of a game, or players can choose them at will if all players agree. It is recommended that only one Mission Modifier and one Achievement should be in effect during any match (unless you really want to get crazy).

name: Name
body: If a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 5" x 5".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 2" x 2". Small obstacles provide cover.

name: Name
body: An elevated platform at least 1" above the table, such as a hill or terrace. Plateaus can possess multiple areas at different heights that models can be placed on, but the areas must be level to prevent models from falling over. If a model cannot be placed on a level area without risk of falling off, it cannot occupy that area. Models cannot be placed on slopes, and we recommend that plateau terrain with sloped surfaces not be used. Hill, Small—A plateau platform with a footprint approximately 6" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 30 mm models to be placed on. Hill, Large—A plateau with a footprint approximately 6" to 12" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 40 mm models to be placed on.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of rubble approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: A 3" x 5" trench template.

name: Name
body: The two scenarios in this installment of Battle Forge utilize the Guard Tower terrain feature. If you don’t have a Guard Tower (or Guard Towers), feel free to substitute or improvise other suitable terrain pieces to stand in for the Guard Towers, but still use the Guard Tower rules (see below).

name: Name
body: Buildings are obstruction terrain features that can be targeted with attacks and destroyed but are not considered to be models and are not friendly to either player. Buildings are placed on the table like any other terrain feature.

name: Name
body:
Buildings can be targeted by attacks like huge-based models. Buildings have DEF 5 and are automatically hit by melee attacks. Buildings gain +4 ARM against ranged attack damage rolls.
Buildings cannot be charged or power attack slammed.
If a building is destroyed, remove it from the table. Any models inside a building when it is destroyed are removed from play.

name: Name
body:
Some building can be entered and occupied. The rules for inhabiting a building are listed on its card.
When a unit enters a building, all models in the unit must be placed inside the building. If there is not room for all the models in a unit to be placed within the building, the unit cannot move into it.

name: Name
body:
Models/units can only exit a building by advancing during their Normal Movement. When a model/unit advances from a building during its Normal Movement, place the moving model in base contact with one of the building’s doors. The model can then make a full advance.
When a unit exits a building, place the remaining models in the unit after the moving model completes its advance as normal.

name: Name
body: If a player has models occupying a building, their opponent cannot enter it.

name: Name
body:
While occupying a building, models gain Resistance: Blast, cannot be targeted or hit by spray attacks, and cannot be knocked down or moved by a slam or push. Models inside a building always have cover.
Opponents cannot take control of models in buildings.

name: Name
body: Models occupying a building cannot engage enemy models or be engaged. They cannot make melee attacks, special actions, or use feats. Models outside a building cannot target models inside it with melee attacks. When measuring distance to or from a model occupying a building to a model outside of the building, measure the range from the foundation of the building closest to the model outside of the building. This includes resolving attacks by models occupying a building targeting models outside of the building or models outside a building targeting models in it. Example 1: A Stormthrower Legionnaire targets an Orgoth Jackal warjack with an Electrical Discharge ranged attack. The range of the attack is measured from the foundation of the building closest to the Jackal. Example 2: Vyros, Incissar of the Dawnguard has the Veteran Leader [Dawnguard] special rule, which says, "While within 10" of this model, other friendly Dawnguard models gain +1 to attack rolls." When measuring distance from Vyros to a Dawnguard Sentinel model inside of a building to determine if the Sentinel is affected by Vyro’s Veteran Leader special rule, measure to the foundation of the building closest to Vyros. If the building is within 10", the Dawnguard Sentinel is affected by his Veteran Leader special rule.

name: Name
body:
If a model inside the Tower is directly hit by an AOE attack, instead of resolving the attack as normal, all other models on the same floor as the target are hit and suffer blast damage from the attack, regardless of the size of the AOE.
A model inside the Guard Tower cannot target another model inside the Guard Tower with an attack for any reason.

name: Name
body: While inside of a building, a model suffers –6 to its Control Range.

name: Name
body: The Guard Tower is an obstruction terrain feature that can be targeted with attacks and destroyed, but is not considered to be a model and is not friendly to either player. The Guard Tower is placed on the table like any other terrain feature. The Guard Tower has the following special rules: Building—This terrain feature is a building. Habitable Guard Tower—Small- and medium-based warrior models can enter this building through a door on the lower level. A model/unit ending its Normal Movement within 1" of the door can choose to enter this building. Models entering this building can be placed on either the lower or upper levels. Models in a unit occupying this building can placed on either floor or both. There can be up to five small-based models or three medium-based models on each floor. There must be room for a model’s base for it to be placed on either floor. Movement Inside the Guard Tower—Models/units can use their Normal Movement to be placed on the top floor if they were previously on the lower floor or to be placed on the lower floor if they were on the top floor. Units using their Normal Movement to be placed are considered to have moved. Models cannot otherwise move or be placed while inside the building.

name: Name
body: Top Floor—The upper level of this building is considered to be elevated terrain. Additionally, arcane and ranged attacks made by models on the top floor gain +4 RNG.

name: Name
body: Encircled by the enemy, one must find and employ an advantage in every element of one’s surroundings to hold the foe at bay. But take heed: the enemy is swift and will let no obstacle slow their advance as they tighten the noose around your neck before help can arrive.

name: Name
body: "Holdout" is designed for 50-point forces.

name: Name
body: "Holdout" ends after seven turns.

name: Name
body: The Defending player begins the game with a reduced force, attempting to defend a lone Guard Tower in the middle of a compound while the enemy attacks from all directions, intent on bringing the tower down. By triggering hazards, the Defender hopes to stall the enemy long enough for reinforcements to arrive.

name: Name
body:
The Defender wants to keep the Guard Tower standing by slowing down and eliminating the enemy.
The Attacker wants to destroy the Guard Tower, whatever it takes.

name: Name
body:
This scenario uses the map layout below. Place a Guard Tower directly in the center of the map, 2 small hills, 4 small forests, 1 large pond, 8 small barriers, 4 small obstacles, and 3 oil barrel moveable objectives on the table as shown. If you don’t have this exact assortment of terrain, use what you have to create a diverse environment outside of the main compound.
Terrain elements should be positioned to define the compound scoring zone, which include the Defender’s deployment zone, so that it’s easy to see at a glance whether or not a model is inside or outside the compound.

name: Name
body:
The Defender gets one small- or medium-based unit (up to 8 PC) and one small- or medium-based non-character solo or Command Attachment (up to 3 PC) for free. These models begin the game inside the Guard Tower. (Note that including the free models in a Force Build will flag it as over the maximum points.)
The Attacker deploys all 50 points of their force amongst as many of the four Attacker deployment zones as they wish.
The Defender must deploy between 20 and 30 points of their force in the deployment zone surrounding the Guard Tower. The Defender’s leader must be included in this deployment. Remaining forces are kept off the table in reserve.
Defenses cannot be placed inside either player’s deployment zones or inside the compound scoring zone.
The Attacker takes the first turn.
At the start of the Defender’s third turn, roll a d6. On a 1, 2 or 3, the Defender deploys their remaining forces from one or more table edges before their Maintenance Phase. On a 4, 5, or 6, the Defender deploys their remaining forces before the Maintenance Phase of their fourth turn.

name: Name
body: Oil barrels are movable objectives that can be picked up by any Cohort model with a medium or larger base that begins, ends, or moves within 1" of the objective during its Normal Movement. A model cannot run while carrying an oil barrel. At the end of its activation, a model carrying an oil barrel can place it anywhere within 1" of its base or it can place a 4" diameter fire field within 1" of its base, then remove the oil barrel from play. If a model is destroyed while carrying an oil barrel, before removing the model from the table, center a 4" diameter Fire Field on the destroyed model’s location.

name: Name
body: Rough Terrain—A Fire Field is rough terrain. Fire Hazard—A Fire Field is a hazard. A model without Flight entering the area of a Fire Field suffers the Fire continuous effect. If a trooper model without Flight advances through a Fire Field as part of its unit’s Normal Movement, all models in the unit suffer the Fire continuous effect. Illumination—Models lose Stealth while within 5" of a Fire Field.

name: Name
body: Beginning with the third round, score 1 Victory Point at the beginning of your turn if you dominate the compound scoring zone.

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Underdog—Beginning with the third round, score 1 victory point at the beginning of your turn if you have fewer models on the table than your opponent. 2. Secure the Area—Beginning with the third round, score 1 Victory Point at the end of your turn if your opponent has no models in the Defender’s deployment zone. 3. Center of the Action—Beginning with the third round, at the beginning of your turn, score 1 Victory Point if your Leader is closer to the Guard Tower than your opponent’s Leader is.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Uneven Playing Field—Once per match, the Attacker scores 3 Victory Points if they destroy all the models on the upper floor of the Guard Tower. The Defender scores 1 Victory Point each time they destroy a cohort model or the last model in a unit by using models occupying the Guard Tower. 2. Bloodletting—Score 1 Victory Point the first time one of your models damages an enemy Leader with an attack each turn. 3. Pyromaniac—Score 1 Victory Point when you place a Fire Field.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win—At the end of any of the Attacker’s turns, if the Guard Tower has been destroyed, they win the match. At the end of any of the Attacker’s turns, if a Fire Field has been placed touching the Guard Tower, they win the match. If at the end of any of the Defender’s turns, all the Attacker’s models have been destroyed, and the Defender has at least one model inside the Guard Tower, the Defender wins the match. Point Advantage Win—At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match. Last Leader Win—At the end of any of the Defender player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match. Victory Point Win—If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match. At the end of seven turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match.

name: Name
body: Darkness is the great equalizer. Within its embrace, friend and foe alike are but shadows until revealed by the light or by their own dying gasps. Strike beneath the shroud of night and snuff the enemy’s light before they can reveal their doom.

name: Name
body: "Deadlights" is designed for 30-point and 50-point forces.

name: Name
body: "Deadlights" ends after six turns.

name: Name
body: Under the cover of darkness, opponents attempt to cross a no-man’s-land to destroy the enemy’s Guard Tower while avoiding searchlights that can give away their position.

name: Name
body: Destroy the enemy’s Guard Tower and as much of their force as possible.

name: Name
body:
This scenario uses the map layout below. Place two Guard Towers, 2 small hills, 4 small forests, 3 rubble fields, 6 small barriers, 4 small obstacles, and 6 oil barrel moveable objectives on the table as shown. If you don’t have this exact assortment of terrain, use what you have to create a diverse environment in the area between the Guard Towers.
Each player also places two 20 mm searchlight markers directly in front of their Guard Tower.

name: Name
body:
Each player can begin the game with up to one small- or medium-based unit and one small- or medium-based solo occupying their Guard Tower.
During a player’s Maintenance Phase, if they have at least one model occupying the upper floor of their Guard Tower, they can move their searchlights. Each searchlight marker can be moved d6+3" in any direction. Models within 2" of a searchlight marker lose stealth and cannot regain it while within 2" of a searchlight.
Oil barrels are movable objectives that can be picked up by any Cohort model with a medium or larger base that begins, ends, or moves within 1" of the objective during its Normal Movement. A model cannot run while carrying an oil barrel. At the end of its activation, a model carrying an oil barrel can place it anywhere within 1" of its base or it can place a 4" diameter fire field within 1" of its base, then remove the oil barrel from play. If a model is destroyed while carrying an oil barrel, before removing the model from the table, center a 4" diameter Fire Field on the destroyed model’s location.

name: Name
body: Rough Terrain—A Fire Field is rough terrain. Fire Hazard—A Fire Field is a hazard. A model without Flight entering the area of a Fire Field suffers the Fire continuous effect. If a trooper model without Flight advances through a Fire Field as part of its unit’s Normal Movement, all models in the unit suffer the Fire continuous effect. Illumination—Models lose Stealth while within 5" of a Fire Field.

name: Name
body: Score 1 Victory Point each time you eliminate a Cohort model, solo, or the last model in a unit.

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Underdog—Beginning with the third round, score 1 Victory Point at the beginning of your turn if you have fewer models on the table than your opponent. 2. Behind Enemy Lines—Score 1 Victory Point at the beginning of your turn for holding your opponent’s deployment zone. 3. Territory Control—Divide the table evenly into four 24" x 24" quadrants. Score 1 Victory Point for every quadrant you dominate at the beginning of your turn.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Uneven Playing Field—Once per match, score 3 Victory Points if you destroy all the models on the upper floor of the Guard Tower. Score 1 Victory Point each time you destroy a cohort model or the last model in a unit, using models occupying the Guard Tower. 2. Bloodletting—Score 1 Victory Point the first time one of your models damages an enemy Leader with an attack each turn. 3. Lit—Score 1 Victory Point when you eliminate an entire unit in a single turn while any model in it is under a searchlight.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win—At the end of any round, if one Guard Tower has been destroyed or is touching a Fire Field and the other Guard Tower is still intact and not touching a Fire Field, the player with the intact Guard Tower wins the match. Point Advantage Win—At the end of any round, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match. Last Leader Win—At the end of any player’s turn, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match. Victory Point Win—If neither player has a Leader in play or if both Guard Towers have been destroyed or are touching Fire Fields at the end of any round, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match. At the end of six turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match.

name: Battle Forge: Holdout & Deadlights - Chapter 1 "Holdout & Deadlights"
